summary: IDF eliminated four Hamas Nukhba commanders in Gaza City's Shati area, including an October 7 infiltrator, while simultaneously striking Hamas operatives in Nuseirat and Daraj Tuffah. Trump declared an "Economic D-Day" on Iran, threatening severe consequences for nations aiding Tehran, as US officials confirmed strikes degraded Iranian radar and maritime surveillance. Mossad chief Roman Gofman contacted Syria's foreign minister before an Israeli strike on Abu ad-Duhur Air Base.
key_points: IDF killed four Hamas Nukhba commanders in Shati, Gaza City, including company commander Muhammad Hamdi Ahmed al-Masri and platoon commander Samad Samir Harb Abu Jabal who infiltrated Israel on October 7. (Source: @New_security8200/203375)

IDF struck a Hamas platoon commander in Nuseirat, central Gaza, who participated in the October 7 attack, and targeted Hamas operatives in Daraj Tuffah planning attacks on Israeli forces. (Source: @New_security8200/203373)

Trump announced the "most crushing economic operation ever" against Iran, declaring "Economic D-Day" and threatening "tremendous economic consequences" for any country supporting Iran financially or logistically. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6418)

US officials stated recent operations were enabled by strikes degrading Iranian radar and maritime surveillance, with US aircraft defending a corridor against Iranian drones and cruise missiles. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6415)

A US source reported the Trump administration reviewed intelligence on an Iranian plan to resume attacks on ships in the Hormuz Strait, with Trump warning of intensive strikes on Iran if economic pressure fails. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/385815)
Mossad chief Roman Gofman spoke with Syria's foreign minister before an Israeli strike on Abu ad-Duhur Air Base in Syria. (Source: @lelotsenzura/94194)
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz warned Erdogan that Israel will not allow any threat to its security from Turkey's actions in Syria. (Source: @yediotnews25/134127)
IDF sealed two additional underground routes in Gaza and conducts "Magen 48" training for defense units in 67 communities near the border. (Source: @New_security8200/203368)

points: Trump announced the "most crushing economic operation ever" against Iran, declaring "Economic D-Day" and threatening "tremendous economic consequences" for any country allowing its financial institutions, companies, airports, or government entities to provide any support to Iran, including oil smuggling, barter lines, cash transfers, exchange offices, ship registries, and shell companies. (Source: @naya_foriraq/88197)

Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi claimed the US has named its next defeat "Economic D-Day" after its military campaign failed, asserting that while the US claims Iran is "hanging by a thread," the US and its allies are actually begging for help to cover up repeated miscalculations. (Source: @presstv/203494)

US officials confirmed that recent operations were enabled by strikes that degraded Iranian radar and maritime surveillance capabilities, with US aircraft now defending a corridor against Iranian drones and cruise missiles. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6415)

A US source reported the Trump administration reviewed intelligence on an Iranian plan to resume attacks on ships in the Hormuz Strait, noting the plan exceeds mere ship targeting, and that Trump informed his team of the possibility of intensive attacks on Iran if economic pressure fails. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/385815)
NATO stated it is ready to respond to any threat from Iran after reports of a possible Iranian attack on Europe, according to the Times of Israel. (Source: @kianmeli1/90930)

Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf met Iraqi President Nizar Amidi in Baghdad and visited the holy shrines of Imam Musa al-Kazim and Imam Muhammad al-Jawad in Kadhimiya, Iraq. (Source: @presstv/203473, @presstv/203487)

IDF struck and killed four Hamas Nukhba Force commanders from the Beit Lahia Battalion in the Shati area of Gaza City: company commander Muhammad Hamdi Ahmed al-Masri, platoon commander Samad Samir Harb Abu Jabal (who infiltrated Israel on October 7), and platoon commanders Muhammad Attar and Muhammad Fathi Hussein Nasser, all involved in planning attacks on IDF troops. (Source: @New_security8200/203375)

Within half an hour, IDF struck a Hamas platoon commander in Nuseirat, central Gaza, who participated in the October 7 attack, and targeted a Hamas commander and additional operatives in Daraj Tuffah who were planning terror attacks against IDF forces operating in Gaza. (Source: @New_security8200/203373)

Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz warned Turkish President Erdogan that Israel will not allow any factor to threaten its security, stating Erdogan is dragging Turkey into dangerous adventures in Syria and should confine himself to parliamentary speeches rather than test Israel's resolve. (Source: @yediotnews25/134127)
IDF's Southern Brigade and Yahalom unit sealed two additional underground routes in the Gaza Strip as part of ongoing subterranean threat neutralization. (Source: @New_security8200/203368)

IDF is implementing the "Magen 48" training program for community defense units in 67 localities near the Gaza border, encompassing live-fire exercises, urban combat in familiar streets, tactical medicine, and joint emergency drills. (Source: @idf_telegram/24932)
IDF closed its investigation into the World Central Kitchen deaths in Gaza, while the inquiry into the killing of Hind Rajab remains ongoing. (Source: @manniefabian/58995)

The Prime Minister's Office clarified that the political echelon did not approve entry of an international force into Gaza, and Israel maintains there will be no reconstruction before Hamas is fully disarmed. (Source: @almogboker78/18008)

IDF struck a police station in Gaza City where at least four Hamas military wing operatives and one Popular Resistance Committees terrorist were gathered to advance attacks on troops stationed in the Strip; Palestinian media reported nine killed and 15 wounded. (Source: @manniefabian/59003)

sections.threat_assessment: The simultaneous IDF decapitation strikes on Hamas Nukhba leadership in Gaza and the escalating US-Iran economic-military confrontation indicate a coordinated pressure campaign. Trump's "Economic D-Day" declaration, coupled with confirmed US strikes degrading Iranian radar and maritime surveillance, suggests a shift from deterrence to active degradation of Iranian capabilities. The reported Iranian plan to resume Hormuz shipping attacks, if executed, would likely trigger the threatened intensive US strikes on Iran. Meanwhile, the Mossad chief's pre-strike communication with Damascus before hitting Abu ad-Duhur Air Base signals Israeli intent to enforce red lines in Syria despite Turkish posturing. Hamas's continued operational planning from Gaza, evidenced by the targeted commanders' involvement in imminent attack preparations, indicates the group retains command-and-control capacity despite leadership losses.
sections.regional_response: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister dismissed US pressure as a failed military campaign rebranded as economic warfare, while Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf's high-profile Iraq visit underscores Tehran's effort to consolidate its regional axis. NATO's stated readiness to respond to Iranian threats to Europe reflects Western concern over horizontal escalation. Turkey faces a direct Israeli warning to curb its Syrian ambitions, creating a potential flashpoint if Ankara tests Israeli red lines. The Lebanese Army's routine disposal of war remnants in Haboush and artillery fire near Hula indicate persistent low-level volatility on the northern border. Iraq continues to serve as a diplomatic conduit for Iranian outreach, hosting both the Iranian Parliament Speaker and presidential-level meetings.
sections.intelligence_notes: The precision of IDF strikes on named Nukhba commanders — including an October 7 infiltrator — suggests high-fidelity human intelligence or signals intelligence penetration of Hamas's command structure in Gaza. The half-hour interval between the Nuseirat and Daraj Tuffah strikes implies real-time targeting cycles. US officials' acknowledgment of degraded Iranian radar and maritime surveillance confirms kinetic action against Iranian sensor networks, likely in Yemen or the Gulf. The Trump administration's explicit linkage of economic sanctions to military threats against Iran, and the warning to third countries, marks a significant escalation in coercive diplomacy. The Mossad chief's direct contact with Syria's foreign minister before the Abu ad-Duhur strike indicates a established communication channel with Damascus, possibly to manage escalation or convey specific warnings. IDF's continued tunnel sealing and expansion of the "Magen 48" program to 67 communities reflect a sustained focus on border defense and subterranean threat mitigation.
